cases.title: FOUNDER NARRATIVE
sectionOutline: Explain the founder’s reason to care.
Show the roles the work requires.

cases.title: TRACTION DIALOGUE
sectionOutline: Define the unit before the headline.
Show the pattern without upgrading it.
Say what is missing about revenue.
Connect a claim to a reviewer question.
Turn the next milestone into a test.
Tie resources to an evidence gap.

cases.title: TECHNICAL THESIS
sectionOutline: State the limits of the mechanism.
Connect the mechanism to a use situation.
Identify the capability needed to build.

cases.title: IMPACT THESIS
cases.framework: 影响路径与商业路径双轨
sectionOutline: Define the problem without claiming representation.
Treat the audience as a research question.
Connect resources to both kinds of uncertainty.

cases.title: ROUNDTABLE BRIEF
sectionOutline: What would the product actually do?
What do you know about the market?
How could the model earn revenue?
Who is responsible for the work?
What are you asking investors to support?

cases.title: LAUNCH KIT
sectionOutline: Give the launch one clear job.
Write for a task, not a stereotype.
Review the release as a system.
Learn without inventing a launch result.

cases.title: CASE STORY
sectionOutline: Set a scene without a success claim.
Describe change without making up a result.
Keep a source trail for every assertion.
Give limitations space in the story.
Extract a useful lesson, not an endorsement.

cases.title: COMPARISON GUIDE
sectionOutline: Describe the options in plain language.
Read the matrix without a score.
Treat cost as an unanswered question.

cases.title: EDITORIAL CALENDAR
sectionOutline: Give the publication a useful purpose.
Build a pool before committing slots.
Make the brief usable by another editor.
Protect review time in the workflow.
Use the review to change the next brief.

cases.title: BRAND VOICE
sectionOutline: Give the voice a practical intention.
Change tone when the situation changes.
Use a tone scale, not a personality score.
Choose words with a clear job.
Do not let familiar slogans hide claims.
Apply the voice in real message shapes.
Keep a change record that explains why.

cases.title: CAMPAIGN PLAYBOOK
sectionOutline: Treat the journey as a hypothesis.
Build assets around the reader’s task.
Coordinate channels without inventing a schedule.
Write replies that respect the question.
Define a measure before collecting it.
Check the points where trust can break.
Close the loop with a useful question.

cases.title: ROLE ONBOARDING
sectionOutline: Understand the role before the checklist.
Map the people around the task.
Observe the task without inventing performance.
Follow one handoff from start to finish.
Use feedback as a gate conversation.
Answer common questions without expanding authority.
Look back at evidence, not completion ticks.

cases.title: SCENARIO PRACTICE
sectionOutline: Practise judgement under an information gap.
Separate the roles in the conversation.
Keep the starting facts in view.
Choose a route and explain why.
Transfer the question, not the fictional outcome.

cases.title: FACILITATOR GUIDE
sectionOutline: Define what the session is for.
Demonstrate the reasoning, not a perfect answer.
Discuss the artifact before the person.
Offer feedback that can be used.
Adjust support without changing the purpose silently.
Close with a question to carry forward.
Review the facilitation, not an imagined result.

cases.title: PEER COACHING
sectionOutline: Agree what peer coaching is not.
Let the speaker describe the situation.
Ask questions that open the task.
Reflect the meaning and check it.
Follow up on the attempt, not compliance.
End deliberately and handle the record.

cases.title: PROCESS REHEARSAL
sectionOutline: Practise the handoff, not a production target.
Check the input before moving it.
Use an exception card for a missing condition.
Record what happens during the exercise.
Discuss a gap without assigning blame.
Propose a revision with a reason.

cases.title: SKILLS PORTFOLIO
sectionOutline: Choose a capability that can be examined.
Break the task into review dimensions.
Plan three attempts with a purpose.
Observe an example without copying its authority.
Keep the first attempt as evidence of a starting point.
Show the revision and its reason.
Organise evidence so a reviewer can inspect it.
